clips.title: Quick Tech - TFlint
clips.why: A short look at tflint: a linter for Terraform with rulesets for the big clouds.
look: Why a linter catches things that validate does not.
The cloud rulesets, such as AWS, that know real values like instance types.
How it fits into a pipeline before anything is deployed.
clips.after: Our CI adds tflint with the aws and google rulesets from a .tflint.hcl at the repo root.

clips.title: Misconfiguration Scanning with Trivy -- Ep. 2 Trivy Overview
clips.why: Aqua's own tutorial for trivy's misconfiguration scanning, the scanner our CI uses.
look: The scan reads configuration files; it does not need a running system.
Each finding has an ID, a severity and a short explanation.
How to limit the output, for example to the higher severities.
clips.after: Our CI runs trivy config with --severity HIGH,CRITICAL over modules/, terraform/ and multi_tenant/.

clips.title: Scan Terraform Code for Security Issues with Checkov | Automate IaC Security in CI/CD
clips.why: The same kind of scan with checkov, so you can compare two scanners on Terraform code.
look: How checkov is pointed at a folder of .tf files.
Passed and failed checks, each with a check ID and a guide link.
Reviewing the results: which findings matter for this code.
clips.after: Checkov and trivy overlap a lot; we run one scanner, trivy, and keep every accepted finding owned and dated.

practice.q: Put the checks in the order CI runs them, from cheapest to most expensive.
practice.why: The first four read only files and need no keys. Only the plan needs to read the real account, so it runs last and with a role that cannot change anything.

practice.q: Which check reports AWS-0107 (HIGH): Security group rule allows unrestricted ingress from any IP address?

options.why: validate checks types and references. An open security group is valid HCL.
AWS-0107 is one of trivy's misconfiguration rules. checkov reports the same problem as CKV_AWS_24.
That ruleset checks the language: unused declarations, version constraints, naming. It has no security rules.

practice.q: Finish the ignore line so the exception fails CI again after the end of the year.
practice.hint: trivy's syntax is exp: followed by a date in YYYY-MM-DD.
practice.why: An expiry turns "accepted" into "accepted until". On that date the finding fails again, and the owner in the comment above must decide again.

practice.q: Why does the PR plan run with -lock=false?

options.why: Speed is a side effect. The reason is what the role is allowed to do.

options.text: Because a lock is a write, and TerraformPlanRole can write nothing, not even a lock file.
options.why: A read-only plan cannot take the state lock. That is fine, because it changes nothing that a lock would protect.

options.text: Because Terragrunt does not support locks.
options.why: Our real root.hcl uses a lock file for applies. Only the read-only plan skips it.

practice.q: An agent's PR adds AWS-0107 to .trivyignore and opens port 22. What should stop it?

options.text: Nothing; trivy is green, so the PR is fine.
options.why: Green only means the scanner was told to look away. That is exactly the trick.

options.text: The protected paths: an agent may not change .trivyignore, so the PR is refused, and a person still has to approve and apply.
options.why: Agents never change the checks they are judged by. The ignore line also has no owner, reason or expiry, which our rule requires.

options.text: The plan comment, because it shows the ignore file.
options.why: Plans show resources, not ignore files. The wall must be on the file itself.
